dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Homogeneous equality: for a type and two objects of that type, it forms the proposition that the two objects are equal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires the real number obtained by squaring sqrtLike x to be exactly equal to x for every real x.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over objects satisfying a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It quantifies over a proposed witness sqrtLike of type Real → Real; the outer negation denies that any such witness has the stated universal property.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous power operation supplied by an HPow instance, taking a base, an exponent, and returning the instance's output type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied with real base, natural exponent, and real output, it forms the power (sqrtLike x)^2 using the displayed power-instance chain.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: It equips a monoid with natural-number powers by mapping x and n to the monoid operation inst.npow n x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the real-number monoid, it interprets the exponentiation in the target as natural-number exponentiation; exponent 2 is the multiplicative square.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the type of the power exponent, specifically the numeral 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Not
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical negation: Not P is the implication P → False.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It negates the entire existential assertion, so the proposition says that assuming the existence of such a function leads to falsehood.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The operation that interprets a natural-number literal in a type having the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 2 used as the natural-number exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is both the domain and codomain of sqrtLike, the type over which x is universally quantified, and the type in which the squared value is compared with x.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The monoid instance on the real numbers, supplying multiplication, the unit, and natural powers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the power operation as ordinary multiplicative natural powering of real numbers, so the second power of sqrtLike x is its square.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: It converts a homogeneous Pow operation with a given exponent type into an HPow operation having the same base and output type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects the real natural-power operation to the HPow syntax used in the equality, preserving a real result.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The natural-number numeral instance that interprets a literal n as the natural number n itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the exponent literal is exactly the natural number 2.

binders: Inside the negated assertion, sqrtLike is existentially quantified over all functions from the real numbers to the real numbers.
For a proposed sqrtLike, x is universally quantified over all real numbers.
conclusions: There does not exist a function sqrtLike : ℝ → ℝ such that (sqrtLike(x))^2 = x for every real number x.
mathematical_definitions: The square (sqrtLike(x))^2 is natural-number exponentiation in the multiplicative monoid of real numbers, hence ordinary real multiplication of sqrtLike(x) by itself.
The outer negation means that the asserted existence of a function with the universal squaring property implies falsehood.
translation.proposition_plain_english: No real-valued function on all real numbers can choose, for every real x, a real value whose square is exactly x.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The required property ranges over every real input, including negative real numbers; it is not restricted to nonnegative inputs.
The witness, if it existed, would have to be real-valued; complex-valued square roots are outside the proposition.
No regularity, sign, uniqueness, continuity, measurability, or principal-root condition is imposed on sqrtLike; only the pointwise squaring identity is required.
The statement only denies a single global right inverse to real squaring on all of ℝ; it does not deny square roots on a restricted domain such as the nonnegative reals.
There is no vacuity from an empty quantified domain: the universal domain is the real numbers and the existential domain is the function type ℝ → ℝ.
